les: 'n Graf wat die rowers gemis het
kaps_punt: Die ontdekking van die graf, wat, wanneer, waarom

items.bewering: 'n Graf wat die rowers gemis het
items.bron: the-past.com, 'Milestones in Egyptology: the discovery and clearance of KV62' (tomb entered by robbers twice in antiquity, robbers' tunnel through the corridor fill, doorways resealed); thecollector.com 'King Tut's Tomb & Howard Carter's Untold Story' (thieves broke in fairly soon after the burial, were caught, and officials resealed the tomb). The lesson's own block 'Waarom die graf oorleef het' also says 'Rowers het kort na die begrafnis ingebreek'.
items.regstelling: Robbers did not miss the tomb: they broke in at least twice soon after the burial, and only LATER robbers missed it. The title must not say that the robbers missed the tomb outright. It should say that later robbers missed it, or say what is true without that claim (for example that the tomb stayed almost whole). As it stands, the title contradicts the lesson's own fourth block.

items.bewering: Vroeëre farao's is in piramides begrawe, soos by Giza in die noorde van Egipte.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Giza' (a plateau southwest of modern Cairo that served as the royal necropolis of the Old Kingdom); UNESCO's 'Memphis and its Necropolis – the Pyramid Fields from Giza to Dahshur' lies in the north, while Thebes lies far to the south. Note: the very first dynasties' kings (at Abydos) were not buried in pyramids, but read as a generic plural for the pyramid age, the claim holds.

items.bewering: Skatte is saam met hulle in die graf gesit.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Tomb Robbing in Ancient Egypt' (grave goods buried with the king were the reason tombs were robbed); Smithsonian Magazine, 'Discover the hidden history of tomb robbing in ancient Egypt'.

items.bewering: Die groot piramides het grafrowers van ver af gelok
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Tomb Robbing in Ancient Egypt', and Live Science, 'Did ancient Egyptians really booby-trap the pyramids?' (the pyramids' size and visibility marked the burial and its treasure, making them obvious targets). Confirmed in the reading 'visible from far away, so they drew robbers'. No source says robbers TRAVELLED from far away; if a learner could take it that way, that reading is unsupported.

items.bewering: en die meeste is lankal geplunder.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Giza' (the Great Pyramid probably opened and robbed by the First Intermediate Period; the pyramids broken into and robbed); Ahram Online, Zahi Hawass, 'The wonders of the Great Pyramids' (the interior of the Great Pyramid was thoroughly robbed in antiquity). 'Die meeste' is, if anything, cautious.

items.bewering: Latere farao's het versteekte grafte gekry wat diep in die rots gekap is.
items.bron: National Geographic, 'Valley of the Kings, Egypt' (New Kingdom kings cut their tombs into the cliff rock, with concealed entrances); UNESCO 'Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis' (the valley was the main burial place of New Kingdom royalty). True of the New Kingdom pharaohs, Tutankhamun's period, as a generic plural.

items.bewering: Dit was waarskynlik deels om rowers weg te hou.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Tomb Robbing in Ancient Egypt', and National Geographic, 'Valley of the Kings' (security is the usual explanation; other sources add religious reasons such as the pyramid-shaped peak above the valley). The hedge 'waarskynlik deels' matches the state of the evidence.

items.bewering: Hierdie grafte lê in die Vallei van die Konings, naby Thebe, verder suid langs die Nyl.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage List, 'Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis' (the site lies within modern Luxor; the Valley of the Kings is on the west bank and was the main New Kingdom royal burial place); Giza lies southwest of Cairo, far to the north (World History Encyclopedia, 'Giza').

items.bewering: Daar is meer as 60 grafte, maar nie almal vir farao's nie.
items.bron: ARCE Cairo, 'The Valley of the Kings' (64 numbered royal and private tombs, KV 64 being the latest, belonging to a singer of Amun); Theban Mapping Project, 'Tomb numbering systems, Valley of the Kings' (KV 62, 63 and 64 the most recent). Counts given range from 63 to 65; 'meer as 60' holds for all of them.

items.bewering: Tog het rowers ook die meeste daarvan geplunder.
items.bron: National Geographic, 'Valley of the Kings, Egypt' (nearly all known royal tombs in the valley were probably robbed before the end of the 20th Dynasty).

items.bewering: In die vallei is voorwerpe gevind met die naam van farao Toetankamen (in Engels: Tutankhamun). Maar sy graf was nog nie gevind nie.
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum of Art collection entries for objects from Tutankhamun's embalming cache (KV54, found by Davis's team, linen inscribed with the king's name); the-past.com, 'Tutankhamun before Tutankhamun' (a faience cup with his name, found 1905/6, and gold foil with his name from KV58, 1909; none of it was his tomb).

items.bewering: Die Britse argeoloog Howard Carter het daarom jare lank daarna gesoek.
items.bron: Griffith Institute, Oxford, 'Howard Carter' (British Egyptologist and archaeologist; spent the winters of 1917 to 1922 searching the Valley of the Kings); the-past.com, 'Tutankhamun before Tutankhamun' (Carter reasoned from the embalming cache that the king's tomb was still waiting to be found in the valley), which supports the 'daarom'.

items.bewering: Op 4 November 1922 het sy span die eerste trede van 'n kliptrap gevind.
items.bron: Griffith Institute, Oxford, '1st Season (1922–1923)' (4 November 1922: the top step of a sunken staircase cut into the bedrock uncovered); Live Science, 'Archaeologists discover King Tut's tomb, Nov 4, 1922'. A step cut in bedrock is fairly called a stone stair.

items.bewering: Later daardie maand het Carter vir die eerste keer na binne gekyk.
items.bron: Griffith Institute, Oxford, '1st Season (1922–1923)' (26 November 1922: Carter made a small breach and looked in by candlelight); Encyclopedia.com, 'Howard Carter' (26 November 1922, 'the day of days').

items.bewering: Die graf was byna ongeskonde en vol duisende voorwerpe.
items.bron: TheCollector, 'What to Look for in the King Tut Galleries at the GEM' (the Grand Egyptian Museum shows all 5,398 objects from the burial); the-past.com, 'Milestones in Egyptology: the discovery and clearance of KV62' (robbed twice, but most of the treasure survived). 'Byna ongeskonde' is the right strength.

items.bewering: Rowers het kort ná die begrafnis ingebreek, maar nie by die farao se sarkofaag gekom nie.
items.bron: thecollector.com, 'King Tut's Tomb & Howard Carter's Untold Story' (thieves got in fairly soon after the burial, were caught, and officials resealed the tomb); Griffith Institute photographic record (seal intact on a golden shrine around the sarcophagus in the burial chamber); the-past.com, 'Milestones in Egyptology' (robbers tunnelled through the corridor fill; doorways resealed in antiquity).

items.bewering: Die graf was klein, en sy ingang het later onder rommel gelê.
items.bron: Theban Mapping Project, 'KV 62 Tutankhamen' (debris already dumped over the entrance before KV 9 was cut, and then KV 9's spoil on top); TheCollector, 'King Tut Galleries at the GEM' (a four-room tomb, small for a pharaoh).

items.bewering: Nog later het werkers se hutte ook daar gestaan. Daarom het latere rowers die graf gemis
items.bron: Theban Mapping Project, 'KV 62 Tutankhamen' (workmen's huts built over the debris during work on Ramesses VI's tomb, KV 9, more than 150 years after the burial, covered the entrance and saved it from the robberies that followed); Griffith Institute, '1st Season (1922–1923)' (Carter found the staircase while clearing ancient workmen's huts). The order in the lesson, rubble first and huts later, matches the sources.

items.bewering: tot Carter dit meer as 3 000 jaar ná die begrafnis gevind het.
items.bron: Tutankhamun's reign is generally dated to about 1332 to 1323 BC (e.g. TheCollector, GEM galleries article; World History Encyclopedia), so burial about 1323 BC to discovery in 1922 is about 3 240 years.

items.bewering: Egipte langs die Nyl. Die kaart wys Giza in die noorde, waar die piramides staan, en die Vallei van die Konings naby Thebe, verder suid. Dit moet duidelik wees dat die vallei suid van Giza langs die Nyl lê, en dat Toetankamen se graf in die vallei gevind is.
items.blok: kaart (vir: Grafte diep in die rots)
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Giza' (southwest of Cairo, in the north); UNESCO, 'Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis' (Luxor and the west-bank Valley of the Kings, far south up the Nile); Griffith Institute, '1st Season' (KV 62 found in the Valley of the Kings).

items.bewering: grafrower: Iemand wat by 'n graf inbreek om die kosbare goed te steel.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Tomb Robbing in Ancient Egypt' (tomb robbers broke into burials to take the valuables buried with the dead).

items.bewering: plunder: Om 'n plek te beroof en die kosbare goed daaruit weg te dra.
items.bron: General dictionary sense of plunder/plunder (to rob a place of its valuable goods), matching usage in World History Encyclopedia, 'Tomb Robbing in Ancient Egypt'.

items.bewering: Vallei van die Konings: 'n Droë vallei naby Thebe waar latere farao's in rotsgrafte begrawe is.
items.bron: UNESCO, 'Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis' (a desert valley on the west bank at Luxor/Thebes, main burial place of New Kingdom royalty); National Geographic, 'Valley of the Kings' (tombs cut into the cliff rock).

items.bewering: argeoloog: Iemand wat dinge van lank gelede soek en ondersoek om uit te vind hoe mense geleef het.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Archaeology' (the study of the human past through the material remains people left behind); Vocabulary.com, 'archaeologist' (studies human history by digging up remains and artifacts).

items.bewering: sarkofaag: 'n Groot kis, gewoonlik van klip, waarin 'n mummie gesit is, dikwels binne-in nog 'n kis.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Sarcophagi' (a sarcophagus is a stone coffin or a container that holds a coffin); Tutankhamun's quartzite sarcophagus held three nested coffins (New World Encyclopedia, 'Sarcophagus', and the nested-coffin descriptions found with it).

items.bewering: ongeskonde: Heel en onbeskadig, sonder dat iets weggevat of stukkend gemaak is.
items.bron: A definition of the word, not a claim about the tomb; the lesson applies it as 'byna ongeskonde', which the sources on the tomb support (robbed twice, yet most of the 5,398 objects survived; see the-past.com, 'Milestones in Egyptology').

opsomming: Every claim in the body text, the map block and the glossary checks out (dates 4 and 26 November 1922, more than 60 tombs, more than 3 000 years, robbers who broke in soon after the burial but never reached the sarcophagus, the rubble and workmen's huts that hid the entrance); the one fault is the title, which says the robbers missed the tomb when robbers broke in at least twice soon after the burial, as the lesson's own fourth block says, so the title must say that later robbers missed it or drop that claim.
